reason: The cited evidence (E1, E2) describes strength-ductility improvements via thermomechanical processing and dual-phase microstructures in CoCrNiV and AlCoCrFeNi2.1, but neither study involves HfZrTiTa0.53 or refractory high-entropy alloys, nor do they address impact energy release. The premises are therefore unsupported by the specific prior evidence provided.
premises: Cold rolling and annealing can refine microstructure in refractory high-entropy alloys to a dual-phase state.
A refined dual-phase microstructure enhances dislocation storage and strain hardening.
Enhanced strain hardening delays plastic instability and increases uniform elongation.
Yield strength can be maintained after thermomechanical processing.
Impact-triggered energy release is preserved after microstructural refinement.
